text: Mercado Bitcoin confirms cyberattack, Hypernative estimates over $40M suspected losses Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed on November 2 that one of its systems had suffered a cyberattack. The exchange said the incident was quickly contained, customers would not incur losses, and no customer data had been leaked. Deposits and withdrawals have been temporarily suspended as a precaution. Tether said it has frozen more than 4.5M USDT related to this security incident. According to preliminary analysis by blockchain security firm Hypernative, more than $40 million in suspicious transfers were identified across at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and Tron. The estimated losses have not been confirmed by the exchange, and the attack method remains unknown. Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin said approximately $38 million in assets were involved in the security incident. Working with Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1, and Chainalysis, the exchange has blocked approximately $11 million and identified additional assets that may be eligible for blocking. Containment efforts remain ongoing. Mercado Bitcoin reiterated that customers will not suffer asset losses and said services will resume once security conditions are fully met, with no timeline announced. — link

Tuesday's midterms are priced at 47 vol, and Brent settled at $117.63 on Friday before easing to $109.66 as Iran–Qatar talks continued.
